site.name: SismoAtlas
site.tagline: Earthquake activity in Morocco and worldwide
site.description: Live earthquakes in Morocco, major earthquakes worldwide, analyses and explainers, with a focus on the Rif.
section.majorEarthquakes.intro: The major earthquakes that shaped Morocco and its region: context, data, aftershocks and lessons learned.
section.understand.intro: The basics to understand why Morocco shakes and how to read earthquake information.
section.factCheck.intro: Short, sourced answers to the misconceptions that spread after an earthquake.
section.reports.intro: Reports prepared automatically from public data, then checked by the team before publication.
section.map.intro: The full seismicity map, with advanced filters and geological layers.

live.usual: The region regularly records small earthquakes, most of them not felt: this is the usual activity of the contact zone between the African and Eurasian plates. SismoAtlas makes no forecasts.

quake.depth.help: Depth of the focus. Shallow: less than 70 km; intermediate: 70 to 300 km; deep: more than 300 km. A shallow earthquake is usually felt more strongly near the epicentre.

world.pager.help: USGS PAGER alert level: an automatic estimate of likely human and economic losses, published within hours of the earthquake and subject to revision.
world.tsunami.help: Strong offshore earthquake: warning centres may issue tsunami information. This USGS flag does not mean a tsunami occurred; follow local authorities.
